questions.learningObjective: state the formula for the magnitude of a cross product
questions.stem: Note TN-4101 tells the translator to render the sentence that states how the size of a cross product is obtained.

options.text: The magnitude equals the product of the two lengths times the sine of the angle
The magnitude equals the product of the two lengths times the cosine of the angle

options.text: The magnitude equals the sum of the two lengths times the sine of the angle
options.misconception: adds the lengths instead of multiplying them

options.text: The magnitude equals the product of the two lengths with no angle factor at all
options.misconception: omits the angle factor entirely

questions.explanation: The magnitude of a cross product is the product of the two lengths times the sine of the angle between them. Using the cosine gives the dot product instead.

questions.learningObjective: identify the base and height of a spanned parallelogram

The base is one length and the height is the other length times the cosine
options.misconception: takes the cosine where the sine is required

options.text: The base and the height are both half the length of the diagonal
options.misconception: invents a diagonal rule that has no basis

questions.explanation: The parallelogram area is one side times the perpendicular height, and the height is the other side times the sine of the angle. The cosine would give the length of the projection instead.

questions.explanation: Expanding the determinant gives the triple (2,-1,1), so the third coordinate is 1. Reversing the order of the two vectors would change that entry to -1.

options.misconception: adds the lengths of two arrows that lie along one line

options.text: A vector perpendicular to the drawn line with the larger arrow length
options.misconception: invents a perpendicular output for parallel inputs

options.text: The zero vector, because the two arrows share the same direction
A vector along the drawn line with the difference of the two lengths
options.misconception: confuses the difference of the lengths with a cross product

questions.explanation: The magnitude of a cross product is the product of the lengths times the sine of the angle, and the sine of zero or a hundred eighty degrees is zero. Parallel arrows therefore give the zero vector.

questions.learningObjective: correct a mixed product in a translated sentence

options.text: The cross product of the last two vectors, taken with the first
options.misconception: reverses the grouping in a way that changes the value

options.text: The magnitude of the first vector times the angle to the other two
options.misconception: describes a partial product rather than a triple product

options.text: The dot product of the first vector with the cross of the other two

questions.explanation: The scalar triple product is formed by taking the cross product of two vectors and dotting the result with the third, which equals a determinant. Any other grouping changes the value.

questions.explanation: The volume is the absolute value of the scalar triple product, and this determinant works out to 2. The same determinant without the absolute value is the signed version, which depends on the order.

Their scalar triple product is one, so they span three dimensions exactly
options.misconception: claims a vanishing volume appears when the volume is full

options.text: Their three pairwise cross products are all parallel to each other
options.misconception: confuses coplanarity with a shared direction

options.text: Their magnitudes satisfy the triangle inequality for the three of them
options.misconception: invents a length test that says nothing about coplanarity

questions.explanation: The absolute scalar triple product is the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by the three vectors. Magnitude inequalities do not detect coplanarity.

Take the point and add the normal to get a second point on the plane
options.misconception: treats a point plus a vector as a plane description

options.text: Take the point and the normal, and keep only the point that is fixed
options.misconception: reduces the construction to a single point

questions.explanation: A normal vector fixes the direction perpendicular to the plane, and one point fixes where the plane sits. Adding a normal to a point gives only another point.

options.text: The product of the two lengths times the sine of the angle
options.misconception: gives the parallelogram area rather than the triangle area

options.text: Half the product of the two lengths times the cosine of the angle
options.misconception: uses the cosine where the sine belongs

options.text: Half the product of the two lengths times the sine of the angle
The product of the two lengths divided by the sine of the angle
options.misconception: divides by the angle factor instead of multiplying

questions.explanation: The triangle spans half of the parallelogram formed by the same two vectors, so its area is one half of the product of the lengths times the sine. Dropping the half keeps the parallelogram area.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: correct a swapped order in a cross product
questions.stem: Note TN-4110 reports that a translated sentence reversed the order of the vectors in a cross product, and asks what change that makes.

options.text: No change, because the cross product is symmetric in its two inputs
options.misconception: believes the cross product is symmetric like a dot product

options.text: The magnitude changes, but the direction of the result stays the same
options.misconception: claims the direction survives a swap of the inputs

options.text: The result becomes the zero vector, since the inputs now match
options.misconception: confuses reordering with making the inputs parallel

options.text: The result is negated, so the direction reverses and the size is unchanged

questions.explanation: The cross product is antisymmetric, so reversing the two inputs negates the whole vector. The magnitude is unaffected, and the result is not zero unless the inputs are parallel.
questions.hint: Swapping the inputs flips the sign of the result.

questions.learningObjective: name the determinant form of the scalar triple product

options.text: The determinant of the matrix whose rows are the three vectors
The product of the three magnitudes divided by the volume

options.text: The magnitude of the cross product of the last two vectors alone
options.misconception: drops the third vector from the triple product

options.text: The sum of the three pairwise dot products of the vectors
options.misconception: adds pairwise dot products instead of forming a determinant

questions.explanation: The scalar triple product is the determinant of the matrix formed from the three vectors. A sum of pairwise dot products is a different quantity.

questions.learningObjective: correct a mistranslated geometric quantity

options.text: Replace the word volume with the word mass, since the value is a weight
options.misconception: swaps in an unrelated physical quantity

options.text: Replace the word area with the word volume, since it measures three dimensions
Replace the word parallelepiped with the word rectangle, which is familiar
options.misconception: swaps the solid for a flat shape and keeps the error

options.text: Replace the word area with the word length, since the value is one number
options.misconception: reduces a three-dimensional volume to a single length

questions.explanation: The absolute scalar triple product is the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by the three vectors, so the area of that solid is the two-dimensional face. The correction is the word volume.

options.misconception: makes the normal parallel to the vectors inside the plane

options.text: The normal is the sum of the vectors that lie inside the plane
options.misconception: builds the normal by adding vectors in the plane

options.text: The normal is perpendicular to every vector that lies inside the plane
The normal is parallel to the plane, since both describe the same set
options.misconception: treats the normal as lying inside the plane

questions.explanation: A normal vector is perpendicular to the plane, hence perpendicular to every direction lying in that plane. It is never parallel to the plane or to the vectors inside it.

options.text: Nothing is missing, because the angle factor is at most one
options.misconception: confuses the dot product bound with the cross product

options.text: The angle factor is missing, since the sine must appear as well
options.misconception: treats the omission of the angle as the only error

options.text: The sum of the two lengths is missing, since the bound is a sum
options.misconception: replaces a valid product bound with a sum

options.text: The sine factor is missing, and it makes the bound sharper

questions.explanation: The magnitude is the product of the lengths times the sine of the angle, and the sine never exceeds one. Stating the sharper form needs the sine.

questions.learningObjective: state the sign rule for a reversed cross product

Reversing the two vectors changes only the sign of the middle component

options.text: Reversing the two vectors changes the sign only when they are perpendicular
options.misconception: restricts the sign change to one special angle

options.text: Reversing the two vectors leaves the result unchanged for any angle
options.misconception: denies the antisymmetry of the cross product

questions.explanation: Antisymmetry means every component changes sign when the inputs are swapped, which is exactly what the right-hand rule reversal shows. The rule holds for every angle, perpendicular or not.
questions.hint: The sign comes from the order of the pair.

questions.learningObjective: explain why opposite vectors give a zero cross product

options.text: Because opposite arrows have the same magnitude, so the difference vanishes
options.misconception: gives a length argument instead of an angle argument

options.text: Because the angle between them is a hundred eighty degrees and its sine is zero
Because opposite arrows describe the same line, so no plane is formed

options.text: Because the right-hand rule gives no thumb direction for opposite arrows
options.misconception: invents a failure of the right-hand rule that does not exist

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: explain why a volume does not depend on the vector order

options.text: Because the volume is a product of lengths, and products of lengths do not care about order

options.text: Because any permutation of the vectors describes the same solid
options.misconception: claims a swap leaves the solid unchanged in orientation

Because the volume is defined to be the largest of the three possible values
options.misconception: invents a maximum-over-permutations definition

questions.explanation: The volume is the absolute value of the scalar triple product, and taking the absolute value removes the orientation sign that a swap introduces. The set of vectors, and hence the solid, is unchanged.

options.misconception: gives a half-truth as a full correction

options.misconception: replaces one error with a claim of mutual parallelism

options.text: The conclusion is wrong, since three coplanar vectors can still be independent

options.misconception: claims right angles make the vectors dependent

options.misconception: ignores the shorter side and the angle

questions.explanation: A normal fixes the direction of the plane, and the offset along that normal is what varies, so a single normal defines a whole family of parallel planes. One point selects exactly one of them.
questions.hint: The normal fixes the direction, not the offset.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: relate the spanned area to a cross product magnitude
questions.stem: Note TN-4133 asks for the relationship between the area spanned by two vectors and the magnitude of their cross product.

options.text: The area is the square root of the magnitude of the cross product
options.misconception: takes a root of a quantity that is already an area

options.text: The area is the magnitude of the cross product times the length of one vector
options.misconception: multiplies by an extra length that is not part of the area

options.text: The area equals the magnitude of the cross product of the two vectors
The area is the magnitude of the dot product of the two vectors
options.misconception: confuses the area with the quantity the dot product measures

questions.explanation: The magnitude of the cross product is the base length times the perpendicular height, which is exactly the parallelogram area. The dot product measures a different product entirely.
questions.hint: Cross product magnitude and area are the same number.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: state what determines the sign of a cross product
questions.stem: Note TN-4134 asks a translator to state the sign convention when two vectors are reversed in a cross product.

options.text: The sign of the result is the sign of the angle, which never changes
options.misconception: ties the sign to the angle instead of the order

options.text: The sign of the result is the sign of the two lengths, which are positive
options.misconception: derives the sign from positive quantities only

options.text: The sign of the result is always positive, since lengths enter the formula
options.misconception: ignores that the order of the vectors also enters

options.text: The sign of the result follows the order in which the vectors are written

questions.explanation: Lengths and sines are nonnegative, so the sign of a cross product comes only from the orientation of the pair, that is from their order. Reversing the order flips that sign.
questions.hint: Lengths are positive, so the order decides.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: state what a zero triple product implies
questions.stem: Note TN-4135 gives the three vectors (1,2,3), (2,-1,0) and (3,1,3) and asks for the value of their scalar triple product.
questions.explanation: The third vector is the sum of the first two, so the three lie in one plane and the determinant vanishes, giving 0. That is exactly the coplanarity test: a zero triple product.
questions.hint: Compute the determinant of the three vectors.

questions.learningObjective: compute the magnitude of a scaled parallel vector
questions.stem: Note TN-4136 says the vectors (1,2,2) and (2,4,4) are parallel, and asks for the magnitude of three times the first of them.
questions.explanation: The first vector has magnitude equal to the square root of 1 plus 4 plus 4, which is 3, and scaling by three gives a magnitude of 9. Parallel vectors keep the same direction and still cross to zero.
questions.hint: Scale the length of the first vector by the factor.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: relate the triple product to the determinant of the three vectors
questions.stem: Note TN-4137 asks which statement explains why the scalar triple product of three vectors equals the determinant of the matrix whose rows are those vectors.

options.text: The determinant expands into the same three products, so the two forms agree
The determinant is a different quantity that only shares the sign
options.misconception: treats the two forms as unrelated results

options.text: The determinant applies only when the rows of the matrix are orthonormal
options.misconception: invents an orthonormality requirement for determinants

options.text: The determinant agrees only when the three vectors are coplanar
options.misconception: restricts the agreement to the degenerate case

questions.explanation: Expanding the determinant along its first row produces exactly the same three products as the triple product. No special condition on the vectors is needed.
questions.hint: Expand the determinant along its first row.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: correct a volume that ignores the angles between the edges
questions.stem: Note TN-4138 reports a translation that computed a parallelepiped volume by multiplying the three edge lengths and ignoring the angles, and asks for the correction.

options.text: The computation is fine, since a box has the same volume as a slanted solid
options.misconception: accepts a false equality between a box and a slanted solid

options.text: The angle factor is missing, so the value overstates the true volume
The computation is fine, because the edges are perpendicular by convention
options.misconception: assumes a parallelepiped always has perpendicular edges

options.text: The computation should be doubled, to account for both bases
options.misconception: invents a doubling rule for parallelepiped volumes

questions.explanation: The volume is the base area times the height, and the base area already contains the sine of the angle between the base edges. The fix is the angle factor, not a doubling.
questions.hint: The base area carries the angle factor.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: compute a cross product of coplanar vectors
questions.stem: Note TN-4139 says the vectors (1,2,0) and (0,1,0) lie in the plane z equals 0, and asks for the magnitude of their cross product.
questions.explanation: The cross product of those two vectors is the unit vector in the z direction, so its magnitude is 1. Coplanarity kills the triple product of three vectors, not the cross product of two of them.
questions.hint: Use the determinant of the two planar vectors.

options.text: The arrow is the direction of the longest line lying in the plane
options.misconception: confuses a normal with a longest direction in the plane

options.text: The arrow is perpendicular to the plane and fixes its orientation
The arrow is the height of the solid built on the marked point
options.misconception: describes a height rather than a normal direction

questions.explanation: A normal is drawn perpendicular to the plane, and it fixes the plane's orientation without picking a position. The marked point supplies the position separately.
questions.hint: A normal stands at right angles to the plane.

questions.learningObjective: correct a false bound on a cross product

options.misconception: claims the sine factor can exceed one

options.misconception: overcorrects, since the value can equal the product

options.text: Change larger to different, since no comparison holds in general
options.misconception: denies a valid comparison that does hold

options.text: Change larger to no larger than, since the sine factor is at most one

questions.explanation: The sine of the angle never exceeds one, so the magnitude of the cross product can never exceed the product of the two lengths. The claim of always being larger is false.

questions.explanation: Those two vectors are perpendicular, so the parallelogram area is 6 times 9, which is 54 square units. The same number is the magnitude of their cross product.

options.text: The result is negated, so the magnitude is unchanged and the direction flips
The result is unchanged, because the two vectors still meet at the same angle
options.misconception: believes the angle alone determines the cross product

options.text: The result becomes zero, because the swapped pair is treated as parallel
options.misconception: claims a swap makes the two vectors parallel

options.text: The result is rotated, so the same magnitude points in a new direction
options.misconception: describes a rotation rather than a sign change

questions.explanation: Swapping the inputs negates the cross product, so the magnitude is preserved while the direction reverses. The angle between the two vectors is unchanged, but the ordering sets the sign.

options.text: It is the zero vector, because a straight angle has a sine of zero
It is perpendicular to the line, with a length equal to the longer vector

options.misconception: invents a doubling rule for collinear vectors

questions.explanation: Taking the cross product of the last two vectors gives the triple (-1,-1,1), and the dot product with the first vector is -2. The absolute value, 2, is the volume of the parallelepiped.

The volume is unchanged, because the base area is unchanged
options.misconception: ignores that the height changed to nothing

questions.explanation: Substituting the point gives d equal to 1 times 2 plus 2 times minus 1 plus minus 3 times 4, which is -12. The sign of the constant follows from the normal and the point given.

options.text: They differ by the sign of the cosine of the angle between them
options.misconception: invents a cosine correction between the two routes

questions.explanation: The determinant components are the perpendicular parts of the two vectors, so their norm reproduces the product of the lengths times the sine. Both routes therefore give the same magnitude.

options.text: It becomes the volume of the triangle formed by the other two vectors
options.misconception: invents a two-dimensional volume for a three-factor product

options.misconception: reduces a determinant to a sum of lengths

options.text: It becomes zero, because the determinant has a zero row

questions.explanation: Taking the cross product of the last two vectors gives the triple (0,2,0), and the dot product with the first is 4, which is the volume. The signed determinant is positive for this ordering.

questions.subject: CALCULUS_II
questions.learningObjective: choose a test for coplanarity
questions.stem: Note TN-4155 asks which statement lets a reader test whether three vectors span a plane or a solid.

options.text: Compute the triple product; zero means they lie in a plane
Compute the pairwise cross products; equal ones mean they lie in a plane

options.misconception: proposes a length test that ignores orientation

options.text: Compute the pairwise dot products; if all vanish they lie in a plane
options.misconception: confuses orthogonality with coplanarity

questions.explanation: The scalar triple product is zero exactly when the three vectors lie in a common plane, so it is the natural test. Pairwise dot products instead measure angles and say nothing about coplanarity.

The parallelogram has one third the area of the triangle
